source: Not findings. Four strategies people actually describe using to reach financial independence. Each is a composition of levers from data/levers.json — the side hustle, the house hack, the steady raise — and every figure lives THERE, not here; this file only says which levers a path pulls and how hard. Every one of them is stated on screen next to the number it moves.
confidenceNote: The paths are a teaching device. No study says a house hack cuts housing by 40% for you; it says it can, and the room lets you change the figure rather than pretending the default is a finding.
note: Read by engines/adventure.js. Never inline a lever figure in a room or in this file: a path is `levers: [{ id, scale }]`, the id a key in data/levers.json and the scale a share of the lever (1 when omitted). The engine composes the raise, the extra income and the housing cut from the levers, and writes each path's assumption sentence from their figures. The house hack reads the real accommodation line (D-172); the share below is a fallback, not a fact. D-174.
returnRateSource: The median real return band in data/return_bands.json, so this room and the rest of the app agree.

paths.label: Steady
paths.line: One job, rising slowly. Save the difference and let it compound.

paths.label: Side Hustle
paths.line: Keep the job, add work of your own on the side.

paths.label: House Hack
paths.line: Attack the largest line instead of the income. Housemate, smaller place, cheaper town.

paths.label: Both, Smaller
paths.line: Half a hustle and half a house hack, because doing two things properly is harder than doing one.

contingencies.label: Markets fall 30%
contingencies.line: A 30% drop in year 2, then the usual return resumes.

contingencies.label: Six months without work
contingencies.line: Income stops for half of year 3. Spending continues.

contingencies.label: Lifestyle creeps up
contingencies.line: Spending rises 4% a year in real terms on top of everything else.

contingencies.label: A real raise
contingencies.line: A 15% rise in year 2 that you keep saving rather than spending.

accommodationShareFallbackNote: Used ONLY when the accommodation line in Cash Flow is blank: housing is taken as 30% of spending, the common rule of thumb, and the room prints "assumed 30% because accommodation is not filled in" beside the figure. With the line filled in the cut reads the real number. D-172.
